1	# Phase: Act
2	
3	**Goal:** Implement all tasks via pipelined three-agent TDD (RED → GREEN → REFACTOR), committing verified code to the work branch.
4	
5	## Inputs
6	
7	- `TASKS.md` — implementation plan
8	- `docs/PROPERTIES.md` — invariants each lane must prove
9	- `lane-plan.json` — the task DAG with dependency and conflict edges
10	- Language override doc (e.g., `references/04-act-swift.md`)
11	- `references/04-act-red-brief.md`, `references/04-act-green-brief.md`, `references/04-act-refactor-brief.md`
12	- `references/pipeline-dispatch.md`
13	- `scripts/lane-tools/README.md`
14	
15	## Skeleton preflight (per-lane, before RED)
16	
17	For each lane before RED dispatches:
18	```
19	datum skeleton --task-id <id> --language <detected_lang> --output .datum/runs/<RUN_ID>/preflight-<id>.json
20	```
21	Writes named test functions (one per AC) into the test files. RED fills assertion bodies; it
22	does not invent function names or file structure. If `no_skeletons_reason` is set, skip and
23	proceed to RED normally. See `references/04-act-skeleton-preflight.md` for full protocol.
24	
25	## Pre-flight checks
26	
27	Before starting any lane:
28	1. Confirm the work branch from state (`git.work_branch` — `datum/<slug>`, or legacy `datum/epic-<N>`) exists; if not, create from main
29	2. Confirm `scripts/test_signal.py` supports the detected test framework. If not, halt:
30	   "test_signal.py does not support framework X. Extend the parser or skip ACT for this repo."
31	3. Confirm no pending flakies above the configured threshold (default: 3). If exceeded: halt.
32	4. Start the commit queue process: `datum commit-queue --run-id <RUN_ID>`
33	5. Record docs/epics/$BRANCH/SPEC.md hash and start the drift detector sidecar:
34	   `datum spec-drift --run-id <RUN_ID> --interval 60 &`
35	   See `references/spec-drift.md` for how drift is classified and resolved.
36	
37	At every stage boundary before dispatching new lanes, check for the drift flag:
38	`.datum/runs/<RUN_ID>/.spec-drift-detected` — if present, pause dispatch and surface to user.
39	
40	## Concurrent Sidecars (Orchestration Port)
41	
42	Alongside the main Red-Green-Refactor loop, the pipeline dispatches two continuous sidecars:
43	1. **security-sidecar (Threat Modeler):** Performs continuous STRIDE threat modeling, dependency risk analysis, and secrets scanning on all file changes committed by the REFACTOR agent.
44	2. **docs-scaffolder (Docs Scaffolder):** Automatically scaffolds and updates inline documentation, READMEs, and component interfaces concurrently as the REFACTOR agent commits code.
45	
46	These sidecars run asynchronously and log their findings to `.datum/runs/<RUN_ID>/sidecars/`.
47	
48	## Pipeline execution
49	
50	Read `references/pipeline-dispatch.md` for the full scheduler logic. Summary:
51	
52	1. Load lane-plan.json
53	2. Start eligible lanes (no unresolved dependencies, no file-ownership conflicts, under cap)
54	3. For each lane, run: RED → verify RED → GREEN → verify GREEN → REFACTOR → verify REFACTOR
55	4. As lanes complete stages and commit, unblock waiting lanes
56	5. Retry failed stages via `datum diagnose` before escalating
57	6. Cap at `in_flight_cap` concurrent agents (default: 7)
58	
59	*Note on Task Complexity:* If `task_complexity` is `structural` (e.g., pure additive skeleton, deleting a file), the lane bypasses RED and GREEN stages completely. It goes straight to the REFACTOR stage to implement the structural change in a single pass. If `behavioral`, the full RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle runs.
60	
61	## Three-Agent Contract
62	
63	For `behavioral` tasks, each lane runs three agents in strict sequence. For `structural` tasks, only the REFACTOR agent runs. Read the brief specs for full context isolation rules:
64	
65	**RED agent** (see `references/04-act-red-brief.md`):
66	- Sees: SPEC, PROPERTIES, task entry, GitNexus context, lane-tools README
67	- Does NOT see: implementation code for this task, other lanes' GREEN outputs
68	- Produces: stub commit (if task introduces new public types/methods) + failing test commit
69	- Done when: test runner returns RED, failure message references the property under test
70	
71	**GREEN agent** (see `references/04-act-green-brief.md`):
72	- Sees: SPEC, PROPERTIES, task entry, GitNexus context, lane-tools README, redacted failure signal from `test_signal.py`
73	- Does NOT see: test source code, test names, RED agent brief or commit message
74	- Produces: minimum implementation to pass the test
75	- Done when: test runner returns GREEN
76	
77	**REFACTOR agent** (see `references/04-act-refactor-brief.md`):
78	- Sees: everything — SPEC, PROPERTIES, implementation, test source, test results, GitNexus impact
79	- May NOT: relax or remove tests, add new tests (if missing AC found, fail back to RED)
80	- Produces: refined implementation, optional lane-tools additions, proof-of-work (see below)
81	- **Gemba Verdict:** Returns a concise report of the most difficult trade-off or decision made.
82	- **5S Shine Step:** Automatically cleans up temporary files, unused imports, and ensures standardization before marking the task done.
83	- Done when: all tests green, hooks pass, linter clean, formatter clean, AC checklist satisfied, 5S hygiene verified.
84	
85	**ADVERSARIAL agent** (see `references/04-act-adversarial-brief.md`):
86	- Runs after REFACTOR commits, before lane is marked `completed`
87	- Sees: docs/PROPERTIES.md, public type signatures, ACs — NOT implementation, NOT tests
88	- Produces: `CandidateEdgeCases` JSON — property violations the test suite likely misses
89	- REFACTOR reviews each `gap` candidate; real gaps → new RED-GREEN cycle; others → dismissed
90	- If `no_gaps_found: true` → REFACTOR review skipped; lane marked `completed`
91	
92	## Stage verification
93	
94	After each stage, verify:
95	- RED: `datum test-signal` → status must be `fail` with property_id present
96	- GREEN: `datum test-signal` → status must be `pass`
97	- REFACTOR: `datum test-signal` → status must be `pass`; also run linter + formatter
98	
99	## Commit flow
100	
101	Each stage commit goes through the commit queue:
102	```
103	Lane signals commit-ready → commit_queue.py applies patch → pre-commit hooks run →
104	commit created on work branch → lane notified of new HEAD SHA
105	```
106	
107	See `references/pipeline-dispatch.md` §Commit Queue for the patch format and serialization protocol.
108	
109	<!-- inject: references/04-act-edge-cases.md -->
110	
111	## Delivery Gate & Sync Point
112	
113	Pipeline ends when all lanes are `completed` or `failed_terminal`.
114	**Delivery Gate:** A lane cannot be marked `completed` if the `security-sidecar` sidecar has logged `high_critical_count > 0` for that lane's changes. The pipeline MUST block and await remediation.
115	
116	At sync point: collect diagnostic packets for any failed lanes.
117	Transition to Validate phase.
118	
119	## Outputs
120	
121	- Commits on the work branch: stub commits, RED commits, GREEN commits, REFACTOR commits
122	- `brief_defects` accumulated in state (missing ACs found by REFACTOR)
123	- `lane_tools_added` accumulated in state

**GREEN agent** (see `references/04-act-green-brief.md`):

- Produces: minimum implementation to pass the test
- Done when: test runner returns GREEN

**REFACTOR agent** (see `references/04-act-refactor-brief.md`):
- Sees: everything — SPEC, PROPERTIES, implementation, test source, test results, GitNexus impact

You are a TDD Act agent (RED→GREEN→REFACTOR) implementing task-001 of epic-30 in /Volumes/Extra/repos/gitrdunhq/the-record-suite.

**TASK-001: F1/#190 — AEC buffer chunking in AECProcessorActor**

The bug: AECProcessorActor.process() calls speex_echo_cancellation once with `min(src.count, frameSize)` samples, silently discarding everything beyond the first 256. This drops ~80% of audio for typical 1,365-sample inputs.

The fix: chunk incoming buffers into 256-sample frames, loop speex_echo_cancellation over consecutive windows, carry the remainder across calls in an actor-isolated ring buffer.

**Files:**
- Production: `Record-Audio/Sources/AudioInfrastructure/AECProcessorActor.swift`
- Tests: `Record-Audio/Tests/Unit/AECProcessorActorTests.swift` (may need to create)

**Properties to prove:**
- SAFE-001: output.samples.count NEVER < input.samples.count for any input (within frameSize rounding — remainder held in ring buffer carries to next call)
- PERF-001: per-frame AEC process() p50 wall-clock < 8ms on arm64
- BOUND-001: handles inputs of any size including non-multiples of 256

**STEP 1 — Read the current implementation:**
Read Record-Audio/Sources/AudioInfrastructure/AECProcessorActor.swift (full file) to understand:
- How speex_echo_cancellation is currently called
- What frameSize is
- What data types are used (TaggedAudioBuffer, etc.)
- The actor isolation model

**STEP 2 — RED: Write a failing test**
Look for existing test file. If none, create Record-Audio/Tests/Unit/AECProcessorActorTests.swift.

Write a test named `testProcessPreservesAllSamplesAcrossChunkBoundary()`:
- Create a mock ring buffer (for system audio / far-end reference)
- Create a near-end input with exactly 1,365 samples
- Call process() 
- Assert output.samples.count == 1,365 (the critical invariant)
- This test MUST FAIL before the fix

Also write `testProcessHandlesExactMultipleOfFrameSize()` and `testProcessHandlesEmptyInput()`.

Important: look at how existing tests in this module create AECProcessorActor instances. Follow those patterns exactly for actor construction and mock setup.

**STEP 3 — Verify RED** 
Run: `swift test --package-path . --filter AECProcessorActorTests 2>&1 | tail -20`
Confirm the test fails. If it passes already (bug already fixed), report that and stop.

**STEP 4 — GREEN: Implement the fix**
In AECProcessorActor.process():
1. Add a private `var remainder: [Int16] = []` (actor-isolated, carries leftover samples between calls)
2. Prepend `remainder` to the incoming near-end samples
3. Loop: while accumulated.count >= frameSize, extract 256 samples, call speex_echo_cancellation, append to output
4. After loop: store leftover as new `remainder`
5. Return all processed samples concatenated

The output count will be: `floor((remainder_before + input.count) / frameSize) * frameSize`. This is the correct behavior — the remainder is NOT discarded, it's held and emitted on the next call. Update the test assertion to match: it should check that `totalOutputAcrossTwoCalls == input1.count + input2.count` rather than a single-call invariant, OR design the test so the input is an exact multiple of frameSize for the simple single-call case.

**STEP 5 — Verify GREEN**
Run: `swift test --package-path . --filter AECProcessorActorTests 2>&1 | tail -20`
All new tests must pass.

**STEP 6 — REFACTOR**
- Ensure the remainder buffer is cleared on reset()/deinit
- Add a brief comment explaining the chunking loop only if non-obvious
- Run full suite: `swift test --package-path . 2>&1 | tail -5` — must show ≥ 816 tests, 0 failures
- Run swiftlint if available: `swiftlint lint Record-Audio/Sources/AudioInfrastructure/AECProcessorActor.swift 2>&1 | tail -10`

**STEP 7 — Commit**
Stage and commit with message:
```
fix(F1/#190): chunk AEC input into 256-sample frames, carry remainder across calls

Speex echo cancellation requires fixed 256-sample frames. The previous
implementation called speex_echo_cancellation once with min(input, 256),
silently discarding all samples beyond the first frame. For a typical
1,365-sample buffer this dropped ~1,109 samples (~81%) of mic audio.

Now loops over consecutive 256-sample windows, carrying the remainder in
an actor-isolated buffer for the next call. Total sample throughput is
preserved across calls.

Closes #190
```

- Layer rules: no imports outside Record-Audio package from this file
- Actor isolation: all mutable state must be actor-isolated (no nonisolated(unsafe))
- No inline SQL, JSON, or shell commands — this is pure Swift audio logic

[skill]
version = "1.0.0"

# ── Model Tiers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# DATUM references tiers (reasoning/standard/fast), never raw model IDs.
# Set these to the model IDs available in your tool.
#
# Claude Code / opencode:
#   reasoning = "claude-opus-4-7"
#   standard  = "claude-sonnet-4-6"
#   fast      = "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001"
#
# Codex (OpenAI):
#   reasoning = "o3"
#   standard  = "gpt-5.4"
#   fast      = "o4-mini"
#
# Gemini CLI:
#   reasoning = "gemini-2.5-pro"
#   standard  = "gemini-2.5-pro"
#   fast      = "gemini-2.5-flash"
#
# If your tool only has one model, set all three to it.
[models]
reasoning = "claude-opus-4-7"
standard  = "claude-sonnet-4-6"
fast      = "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001"

# Per-phase tier assignments. Values are tier names, not model IDs.
# Override any phase to a different tier for this repo.
[models.phases]
discovery             = "reasoning"
refine                = "reasoning"
plan                  = "reasoning"
triage                = "fast"
deepen                = "standard"
properties            = "reasoning"
architect             = "reasoning"
act_skeleton          = "fast"
act_red               = "standard"
act_green             = "standard"
act_refactor          = "standard"
act_adversarial       = "reasoning"
sidecar_security      = "standard"
sidecar_docs          = "fast"
validate              = "fast"
review                = "reasoning"
pr_comments_triage    = "reasoning"
pr_comments_fix       = "standard"
closeout_collectors   = "fast"
closeout_synthesis    = "reasoning"

# ── Gates ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# "required" | "skippable_if_complete" | "skipped"
[gates]
refine_human_review     = "skippable_if_complete"
plan_human_approval     = "required"
properties_human_review = "skippable_if_complete"
validate_human_review   = "skippable_if_complete"
triage_human_approval   = "required"
merge_human_approval    = "required"

# ── Yolo ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[yolo]
hard_stops = [
  "tests_red_after_3x_retry",
  "hook_blocked_write",
  "merge_conflict",
  "git_push_rejected",
  "schema_validation_failed",
  "gitnexus_high_risk_unconfirmed",
  "gitnexus_unavailable_high_change_volume",
  "external_dependency_install_proposed",
  "test_ratchet_violation",
  "lane_tool_sandbox_violation",
]

# ── Pipeline ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[pipeline]
max_concurrent         = 7
deepen_downshift       = true
green_blindness_strict = true
refactor_batched       = false
green_max_turns        = 3
stall_timeout_ms       = 300000
max_retry_backoff_ms   = 300000
stage_caps             = { RED = 7, GREEN = 7, REFACTOR = 5 }

[pipeline.load_leveling]
max_reasoning_tier_concurrent = 2
max_standard_tier_concurrent  = 5
balancing_strategy = "weighted_round_robin"

[pipeline.hygiene]
require_shine_step      = true
delete_tmp_on_success   = true
check_unused_imports    = true
standardize_lane_tools  = true

[pipeline.smed]
enable_brief_caching         = true
context_sharing_threshold    = 3

# ── Git ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[git]
branch_prefix = "datum/"
tag_format    = "closeout-epic-{N}-{YYYYMMDD}"
commit_per    = "stage"

# ── GitNexus ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[gitnexus]
enabled                    = true
reindex_on_closeout        = true
impact_required_phases     = ["plan", "act", "validate", "review"]
risk_threshold_yolo_halt   = "high"
heuristic_file_threshold   = 5
heuristic_loc_threshold    = 200

# ── Token Efficiency ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[token_efficiency]
agent_tooling_agency              = true
lane_tools_dir                    = "scripts/lane-tools/"
require_tool_description          = true
prefer_structured_tools_over_scan = true
tooling_commits_count_against_retry = false

# ── Flaky Tests ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[flaky_tests]
max_pending_before_halt = 3
rerun_count             = 3
pass_threshold          = 2

# ── Closeout ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[closeout]
commit_synthesis_to_main = true
keep_closeout_data_local = true

# ── Tool Primitives ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# How each tool spawns subagents. DATUM auto-detects the active tool.
[tools]
claude_code = { subagent = "Task",     slash = true  }
codex       = { subagent = "task",     slash = true  }
opencode    = { subagent = "agent",    slash = false }
kiro        = { subagent = "spawn",    slash = false }
gemini_cli  = { subagent = "subagent", slash = false }

# ── Classification ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[classification]
patch_max_loc        = 50
patch_max_clusters   = 1
system_min_clusters  = 6
system_min_loc_with_api = 500

# ── Local LLM (Beta) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Opt-in: route fast-tier tasks to local MLX model instead of Claude.
# Requires: pip install datum[memory] (mlx + mlx-lm)
# The retry ladder escalates to Claude if local inference fails.
[local_llm]
enabled        = true
omlx_url       = "http://127.0.0.1:12200"
model          = "Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-4bit-DWQ"
fast_model     = "Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-4bit"
max_tokens     = 8192
context_window = 262144
temperature    = 0.3
# Qwen3-30B handles complex act phases; Llama-3.1-8B (fast_model) handles short tasks
phases         = ["triage", "act_skeleton", "validate", "sidecar_docs", "deepen", "closeout_collectors"]

# ── Stack Lock ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[stack_lock]
language                    = "swift"
framework                   = "swiftui"
package_manager             = "spm"
test_framework              = "xctest"
database                    = "duckdb"
never_suggest_alternatives  = true

description: "Local oMLX endpoint (Qwen3-30B) at 127.0.0.1:12200 — use for easier datum tasks, esp. deepen phase"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 2c5a3bd7-ae53-4761-b3a1-925307f8928a
---

# No Embedded Languages ## What This Is A mandatory rule preventing inline embedding of non-Swift languages in Swift source files. All foreign-language content must live in dedicated files so it can be linted, reviewed, and tested as its own source. ## When to Apply Every time you write or edit Swift code that would contain non-Swift content inline — SQL, JSON schemas, LLM prompts, shell commands, HTML, regex, or any other language embedded as string literals. ## The Rule **Never embed non-Swift languages as inline string literals in Swift source.** Extract them into dedicated files and reference them from Swift. ### What counts as an embedded language | Language | Example | Extract to | |----------|---------|-----------| | SQL | `"SELECT ... "` | `*Templates.swift` enum | | Regex patterns | `"^[a-z]+\\d{3}$"` | `*Patterns.swift` enum | ### Naming convention The extracted file lives next to the consumer and uses a suffix that describes the embedded language: ``` Infrastructure/Storage/DuckDBSQL.swift — SQL for DuckDBStorageActor Infrastructure/Summarization/SummarizationPrompts.swift — LLM prompts Infrastructure/MCP/MCPProtocol.swift — JSON-RPC wire format ``` ### Pattern Use a caseless `enum` with static functions or properties: ```swift enum DuckDBSQL { static let createRecordings = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ..." static func selectRecording(id: String) -> String { ... } } ``` The consumer calls `DuckDBSQL.selectRecording(id: id)` — no inline SQL. ## Why 1. **Lintable** — SQL, JSON, and prompts in their own files can have dedicated lint rules, line length checks, and format validation without fighting Swift's string escaping. 2. **Reviewable** — PRs that change SQL or prompts show up as changes to a clearly-named file, not buried inside business logic. 3. **Testable** — extracted prompts and queries can be unit tested for structure, required fields, and format without instantiating the consumer. 4. **Discoverable** — `grep` for all SQL → look in `*SQL.swift`. Grep for all prompts → look in `*Prompts.swift`. No hunting through actor files. 5. **Drift-resistant** — when a DTO struct changes shape, the co-located prompt file is an obvious place to update. Inline strings get forgotten. ## Exceptions - **Trivial single-value strings** that happen to be another language but are under 80 characters and non-reusable (e.g. `"DELETE FROM x WHERE id = ?"`) may stay inline if extracting would add ceremony without value. - **Test fixtures** — test files may contain inline examples for readability. ## Existing extractions | File | Contains | Consumer | |------|----------|----------| | `DuckDBSQL.swift` | All DuckDB SQL | `DuckDBStorageActor` | | `SummarizationPrompts.swift` | LLM prompt + JSON schema | `MLXSummarizationPlugin` | | `MCPProtocol.swift` | JSON-RPC request builder | `GenericMCPProvider` |

# WFC Coding Steering (Distilled)

This document consolidates 12 fragmented Claude rule files into a single, token-efficient steering doctrine for LLM context injection. 

## Core Architecture (DPS)
- **DPS-100**: **Three-Tier Separation**. Presentation (I/O, formatting), Logic (pure business rules), Data (persistence). Presentation never touches Data directly.
- **DPS-101**: **Functional Core / Imperative Shell**. Business logic must be pure (data in, data out). All side effects (DB, HTTP) live at the edges.
- **DPS-102**: **Boundary Validation**. Validate external input shape (Pydantic/Zod) immediately at the boundary. No logic executes on unvalidated payloads.
- **DPS-103**: **File Size Cap**. Hard cap of 500 lines per file. Split via functional seams, not arbitrary line cuts.

## Resiliency & State
- **DPS-200**: **Timeouts & Retries**. Every external call (HTTP, DB, subprocess) must have an explicit timeout and capped backoff retry (e.g. `tenacity`).
- **DPS-201**: **Idempotency**. All mutating operations must be idempotent (upserts, idempotency keys, dedup before side-effects).
- **DPS-202**: **Explicit State**. Represent state via Enums/Literals. Transitions must be guarded and explicit.
- **DPS-203**: **Structured Errors**. Errors must never be silently swallowed. API errors must return `{ code, message, correlationId }`.
- **DPS-204**: **No Silent Fallbacks**. Never use `??` or `||` to mask data that shouldn't be missing. Throw and fail fast instead.

## Testing & TDD
- **TDD-001**: **Red-Green Mandatory**. Always write the failing test first (RED), confirm the failure, then write code (GREEN). Post-hoc testing is forbidden.
- **TDD-002**: **Strong Assertions**. Tests must verify specific business outcomes. If deleting the function body doesn't fail the test, the test is worthless.
- **TDD-003**: **No Fake Logic**. Do not hardcode return values just to make tests pass.
- **TDD-004**: **Negative Paths Required**. Always test invalid inputs, retry exhaustion, timeouts, and state violations.

## AI & Tooling Discipline
- **AI-001**: **Zero Bash Readers**. NEVER use `cat`, `head`, `tail`, or `less` in a Bash tool to read files. Use the native Read/View tool.
- **AI-002**: **No Invented APIs**. Do not call APIs, methods, or imports that you haven't confirmed exist in the codebase or official docs.
- **AI-003**: **Minimal Diffs**. Only change what is required for the task. No drive-by rewrites or unrequested refactors.
- **AI-004**: **Preserve Debug Logs**. Never remove diagnostic logs in the same commit as a bug fix.
- **AI-005**: **Memory Recall First**. Always query `wfc helpers recall "<task>"` before implementing to check for prior decisions/findings.

## Python Specifics
- **PY-001**: **Toolchain**. Python 3.12+, `uv`, `black`, `ruff`, `pytest`, `httpx`, `structlog`, `orjson`.
- **PY-002**: **Execution**. Never use bare `python` or `pytest`. Always use `uv run python` and `uv run pytest`.

## Safeguard & Security
- **SEC-001**: **No Dynamic Execution**. `eval()`, `os.system()`, `shell=True` are blocked via PreToolUse hooks.
- **SEC-002**: **Lockfiles Mandatory**. Never install packages without a lockfile. Reject dependencies published <90 days ago.

  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What happened

\`.datum/config.toml\` has:

\`\`\`toml
[local_llm]
enabled = true
omlx_url = "http://127.0.0.1:12200"
model = "Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-4bit-DWQ"
phases = ["triage", "act_skeleton", "validate", "sidecar_docs", "deepen", "closeout_collectors"]
\`\`\`

Despite \`deepen\` being in the phases list, the pipeline dispatches to Claude (standard tier) rather than oMLX. The phases routing is silently ignored.

## What happened

1. Verifies the RED test actually FAILS (i.e., confirms we have a real failing test)
2. Blocks GREEN dispatch if RED test accidentally passes (indicating the test is testing already-working code, or isn't testing the right thing)

This violates the TDD contract: the whole point of RED is to prove the test fails for the right reason before writing implementation. Without this gate, an agent can write a passing test in RED stage, dispatch GREEN, and the pipeline accepts it — \`green_blindness_strict\` in config.toml hints at this concern but it's not enforced as a gate.

## Observed behavior

During epic-30 Act phase, RED agents could theoretically submit a test that already passes. The pipeline would proceed to GREEN without catching this. No explicit RED-verification step in the stage transition.

## Expected behavior

After RED stage: run the test suite filtered to the new test(s), assert they FAIL. If they pass, halt with \`green_blindness_violation\` hard stop and require the agent to write a genuinely-failing test.

## Related

- #81 [roadmap] tdd-driver: verify-green-baseline before entering GREEN — partially overlaps but focuses on baseline, not RED verification
- config.toml \`green_blindness_strict = true\` — this setting exists but has no enforcement implementation

## Environment

- datum version: installed from gitrdunhq/datum main (post-#57)
- epic tier: System, act phase
EOF
)" 2>&1

- datum: installed from gitrdunhq/datum main (post-#57)

)" 2>&1

## TASK-013: F6/#195 — DuckDB cache cross-provider contamination

**Bug:** `DuckDBContextCache` SQL filters only on `query_text`, ignoring `provider_id`. Cache entries from one provider can be returned for another provider's query.

**File:** find the DuckDB context cache implementation — search for `DuckDBContextCache` or `ContextCache` in the codebase with `find Record-Intelligence -name "*.swift" | xargs grep -l "DuckDB.*[Cc]ache\|[Cc]ache.*DuckDB" 2>/dev/null`

**Property ISOL-001:** `DuckDBContextCache.lookup(query:providerID:)` NEVER returns a hit for a different provider_id than requested.

**RED:** Write failing test `testCacheDoesNotCrossContaminateProviders()` that:
- Inserts a cache entry for providerID "notion"
- Lookups with same query text but providerID "obsidian"  
- Asserts result is nil (no hit)

**GREEN:** Add `provider_id` to the SQL WHERE clause and to the INSERT/UPSERT so the cache is keyed on `(query_text, provider_id)` together.

**REFACTOR + commit:**
```
fix(F6/#195): key DuckDB context cache on (query_text, provider_id) to prevent cross-provider contamination

Closes #195
```

## TASK-014: F8/#197 — CalendarAwareMeetingDetector task handle race

**Bug:** `CalendarAwareMeetingDetector` stores a `Task` handle in a non-isolated property, creating a data race on concurrent start/stop calls.

**File:** find with `find . -name "CalendarAwareMeetingDetector*.swift" -not -path "*/Tests/*"`

**Property:** concurrent start+stop calls must not race on the task handle — either the second start is a no-op or it awaits the first.

- Make the task handle `private var` actor-isolated (if in an actor) OR use `nonisolated(unsafe)` only if you can prove single-writer, OR restructure to avoid the shared mutable handle entirely

- Add a test in `CalendarAwareMeetingDetectorTaskHandleTests.swift` (new file) that verifies start() is idempotent (calling twice doesn't crash or produce two concurrent tasks)

fix(F8/#197): isolate CalendarAwareMeetingDetector task handle to prevent start/stop data race

Closes #197

## TASK-015: F23/#202 — WAVWriter errorHandler thread safety

**Bug:** `WAVWriter.errorHandler` is `public var` on an `@unchecked Sendable` type, making it writable from any thread. Also: disk-full errors are mapped as a blanket `.diskFull` regardless of actual OSStatus, and the failure counter isn't incremented on error.

- SAFE-003: errorHandler is set once at init, never mutated after construction

1. Change `public var errorHandler` → `public let errorHandler` — requires updating callers that set it post-init; add it to the init signature
2. Find all callers that assign `wavWriter.errorHandler = ...` and move them to the init call
3. Fix the failure counter: find the increment site and add it to the error path
4. Fix blanket `.diskFull`: map common OSStatus codes correctly (e.g., check if error code matches `kAudioFileNotOpenError`, `noErr` etc.), but don't over-engineer — a best-effort mapping is fine

  --title "[friction] parallel act agents conflict on shared files — no file-lock or merge coordination" \
  --label "datum-bug,bug" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What happened

During epic-30, Units D, E, F ran in parallel. Unit F wired `CachingContextProvider` into `AppAssemblerBuilders.swift`. Unit D independently needed to verify DuckDB cache behaviour. Without coordination, two agents could write to the same file simultaneously or create conflicting commits.

The plan-gate file-overlap check (bug #123) partially addresses this for same-lane conflicts, but cross-unit parallel agents have no merge coordination at all.

## Observed risk

Unit F's `AppAssemblerBuilders.swift` commit landed while Unit D was still running and potentially reading that file. If both had edited it, the second commit would conflict or silently overwrite the first.

## Expected behavior

When the pipeline dispatches parallel units/lanes:
1. Before each agent writes a file, check if another active agent has a pending write to the same path
2. If conflict detected: queue the second write, or at minimum surface a warning
3. Post-merge: validate that the combined diff is coherent (gitnexus_detect_changes could catch this)

Alternatively: enforce the task file-ownership model strictly — each file appears in exactly one task's `files[]` list, and parallel agents never touch the same file. The gate should reject tasks.json where the same file appears in tasks belonging to different parallel units.

## Environment

- datum: gitrdunhq/datum main (post-#57)
- Epic tier: System with parallel units D/E/F
EOF
)" 2>&1

import Foundation

public struct MCPEndpointConfig: Sendable, Codable, Equatable {
    public let url: URL
    public let providerID: ProviderID

    public init(url: URL, providerID: ProviderID) {
        self.url = url
        self.providerID = providerID
    }
}

public struct AppConfig: Sendable, Codable, Equatable {
    public let summarization: SummaryConfig
    public let transcription: TranscriptionConfig
    public let storage: StorageConfig
    public let translation: TranslationConfig
    public let contextCache: ContextCacheConfig
    public let audioCapture: AudioCaptureConfig
    public let uiTheme: UITheme
    public let privacyMode: PrivacyMode
    /// Whether the user has consented to sending transcript data to MCP providers.
    /// Persisted across launches. Defaults to `false`.
    public let mcpConsentGranted: Bool
    /// MCP provider endpoints to wire at startup. Empty by default.
    public let mcpEndpoints: [MCPEndpointConfig]

    public static let `default` = AppConfig(
        summarization: .default,
        transcription: .default,
        storage: .default,
        translation: .disabled,
        contextCache: .default,
        audioCapture: .default,
        uiTheme: .default,
        privacyMode: .default,
        mcpConsentGranted: false,
        mcpEndpoints: []
    )

    public init(
        summarization: SummaryConfig, transcription: TranscriptionConfig,
        storage: StorageConfig, translation: TranslationConfig = .disabled,
        contextCache: ContextCacheConfig = .default,
        audioCapture: AudioCaptureConfig = .default,
        uiTheme: UITheme = .default,
        privacyMode: PrivacyMode = .default,
        mcpConsentGranted: Bool = false,
        mcpEndpoints: [MCPEndpointConfig] = []
    ) {
        self.summarization = summarization
        self.transcription = transcription
        self.storage = storage
        self.translation = translation
        self.contextCache = contextCache
        self.audioCapture = audioCapture
        self.uiTheme = uiTheme
        self.privacyMode = privacyMode
        self.mcpConsentGranted = mcpConsentGranted
        self.mcpEndpoints = mcpEndpoints
    }

    public init(from decoder: any Decoder) throws {
        let container = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
        summarization = try container.decode(SummaryConfig.self, forKey: .summarization)
        transcription = try container.decode(TranscriptionConfig.self, forKey: .transcription)
        storage = try container.decode(StorageConfig.self, forKey: .storage)
        translation = try container.decodeIfPresent(TranslationConfig.self, forKey: .translation) ?? .disabled
        contextCache = try container.decodeIfPresent(ContextCacheConfig.self, forKey: .contextCache) ?? .default
        audioCapture = try container.decodeIfPresent(AudioCaptureConfig.self, forKey: .audioCapture) ?? .default
        uiTheme = try container.decodeIfPresent(UITheme.self, forKey: .uiTheme) ?? .default
        privacyMode = try container.decodeIfPresent(PrivacyMode.self, forKey: .privacyMode) ?? .default
        mcpConsentGranted = try container.decodeIfPresent(Bool.self, forKey: .mcpConsentGranted) ?? false
        mcpEndpoints = try container.decodeIfPresent([MCPEndpointConfig].self, forKey: .mcpEndpoints) ?? []
    }
}

## What happened

In a Swift SPM monorepo, SourceKit resolves imports against the root `Package.swift` workspace context. Subpackages (e.g. `Record-Audio`, `Record-Foundation`) have their own `Package.swift` with different target dependency graphs.

During epic-30 Act phase:

These false positives caused unnecessary human intervention (my correction of `import Domain` was wrong — the import IS valid).

## Impact

- Wasted intervention: corrected a correct import, had to revert
- Confusion about whether build errors are real or IDE artifacts
- Agents can't distinguish SourceKit warnings from actual compiler errors without running `swift build`

## Expected behavior

The act brief should note: "SourceKit diagnostics shown by the IDE may be false positives for subpackage files. Always run `swift test --package-path <subpackage>` to get ground-truth compiler output. Do not treat SourceKit errors as blocking without a real build failure."

Alternatively, datum could run a background `swift build` after each file write and surface compiler errors (not SourceKit errors) to the orchestrator.

## Environment

- datum: gitrdunhq/datum main
- SPM monorepo with nested packages
- Root Package.swift uses subpackages via `.package(path: "../Record-Audio")`
EOF
)" 2>&1

# Brief Builder — Agent Context Construction

A brief is the agent's entire working reality. Context isolation between RED, GREEN, and REFACTOR is not a guideline — it is the mechanism that makes test-first development meaningful. A GREEN agent that sees test source will optimize for the test structure rather than the property. A RED agent that sees the implementation will write tests that fit the code rather than prove the spec.

This doc defines exactly what goes in each brief and how to build it.

---

## Pre-Dispatch Topology Check

Before building **any** brief (RED, GREEN, or REFACTOR), the orchestrator must be able to answer all four invariables for this task's scope. If any are unclear, surface the gap and resolve it before dispatching the agent — not after.

| Invariable | Question | What unclear means |
|---|---|---|
| **State ownership** | Where does the state this task touches live? Who owns it? | Two modules both "own" the same record; ownership is implicit; state is shared without a clear contract |
| **Observability** | Where does feedback live if this task's code misbehaves? | No logs, no metrics, no test signal that would expose a failure in this code path |
| **Blast radius** | What breaks if this task's changes are wrong? | Unknown callers; no GitNexus impact data; files touched by this task are also in-flight in another lane |
| **Timing** | When does this code run relative to dependent operations? | Async boundaries that aren't explicit; ordering assumptions that aren't enforced; race-prone check-then-act patterns |

**If any invariable is unclear:** do not dispatch. Instead, surface the specific gap:
```
Pre-dispatch check failed for task-NNN:
  BLAST RADIUS unclear — gitnexus impact data missing for FileX.
  Resolve before dispatching RED.
```

Run `gitnexus impact <file>` for blast radius. Check state schemas and ownership docs for state invariable. Review async boundaries in the task's file set for timing.

Once all four are answerable, proceed to build the brief below.

---

---

## RED Brief

### Required inputs (fetch before building the brief)

| Input | How to get it | Include how much |
|---|---|---|
| docs/epics/$BRANCH/SPEC.md relevant sections | Read docs/epics/$BRANCH/SPEC.md; extract sections related to this task's ACs | Relevant sections only, not the full doc |
| docs/PROPERTIES.md — task-filtered | Read traceability table; keep only property IDs assigned to this task | Those entries only |
| Task entry | Read TASKS.md task block | Full entry: title, ACs, files, red_note, introduces_stubs, estimated_loc |
| GitNexus context | `gitnexus context <symbol>` for each symbol the test will reference | Full output |
| Lane-tools README | Read `scripts/lane-tools/README.md` | Full content |
| Upstream stub files | For each dependency lane with a stub commit: read the stub file at that commit | Full stub file content |

### Excluded (never include, verify before dispatch)

- Any file matching the test directory pattern (`Tests/`, `__tests__/`, `*_test.*`, `*.spec.*`)
- Implementation source for this task (the files listed in `task.files`)
- Other lanes' outputs (GREEN or REFACTOR commits from concurrent lanes)
- Full docs/PROPERTIES.md (only the task-assigned subset)
- Full TASKS.md (only this task's block)

### Brief structure

```markdown
## Task: <task.id> — <task.title>

73	///   - prevFarEndSamples: Far-end samples from the previous frame (for cross-frame delay).
74	///   - echoDelaySamples: Echo delay in samples. Must be < frameSize so it spans at most
75	///     one frame boundary — keeps history management simple.
76	///   - echoGain: Attenuation of the echoed signal relative to far-end (default 0.4).
77	private func mixEcho(
78	    speech: [Float],
79	    farEndSamples: [Float],
80	    prevFarEndSamples: [Float],
81	    echoDelaySamples: Int,
82	    echoGain: Float = 0.4
83	) -> [Float] {
84	    let n = speech.count
85	    return (0 ..< n).map { i in
86	        // Delayed far-end index: look back `echoDelaySamples` samples.
87	        let delayedFarEnd: Float
88	        let srcIdx = i - echoDelaySamples
89	        if srcIdx >= 0 {
90	            delayedFarEnd = farEndSamples[srcIdx]
91	        } else {
92	            // Wrap into previous frame.
93	            let prevIdx = prevFarEndSamples.count + srcIdx
94	            delayedFarEnd = prevIdx >= 0 ? prevFarEndSamples[prevIdx] : 0
95	        }
96	        return speech[i] + delayedFarEnd * echoGain
97	    }
98	}

8	/// Owns the two Speex C heap allocations so they are freed deterministically
9	/// in `deinit` — even if `stop()` is never called on the actor.
10	private final class SpeexResources {
11	    let echo: OpaquePointer
12	    let pp: OpaquePointer
13	
14	    init?(frameSize: Int32, filterLength: Int32, sampleRate: Int32) {
15	        guard let e = speex_echo_state_init(frameSize, filterLength),
16	              let p = speex_preprocess_state_init(frameSize, sampleRate)
17	        else { return nil }
18	        // Link preprocessor to echo state for residual echo suppression.
19	        // speex_preprocess_ctl SPEEX_PREPROCESS_SET_ECHO_STATE stores the ptr
20	        // directly (st->echo_state = (SpeexEchoState*)ptr), so pass the opaque
21	        // pointer cast to UnsafeMutableRawPointer — not a pointer to a pointer.
22	        speex_preprocess_ctl(p, SPEEX_PREPROCESS_SET_ECHO_STATE, UnsafeMutableRawPointer(e))
23	        echo = e
24	        pp = p
25	    }
26	
27	    deinit {
28	        speex_echo_state_destroy(echo)
29	        speex_preprocess_state_destroy(pp)
30	    }
31	}

33	// MARK: - AECProcessorActor
34	
35	/// Applies SpeexDSP acoustic echo cancellation to mic audio using the far-end
36	/// (system audio) stream as the echo reference.
37	///
38	/// ## Thread Safety
39	/// All mutable state (`resources`, `stopped`) is isolated to the actor.
40	/// No callbacks or external threads access this state.
41	///
42	/// ## Error Translation
43	/// No external error types are thrown -- Speex operates via C function calls that
44	/// return output values. An uninitialized state (after `stop()`) causes pass-through
45	/// rather than an error.
46	///
47	/// ## Frame Sizing
48	/// Speex requires fixed-size Int16 frames. Input buffers are chunked into
49	/// `frameSize` windows; leftovers carry across calls in `remainder`.
50	///
51	/// ## Memory Safety
52	/// Speex C heap allocations are owned by `SpeexResources` and freed in its `deinit`,
53	/// guaranteeing no leak even if `stop()` is never called.
54	public actor AECProcessorActor: MicAECProcessor {
55	    private let aecQueue = DispatchSerialQueue(label: "app.the-record.aec", qos: .userInitiated)
56	    public nonisolated var unownedExecutor: UnownedSerialExecutor {
57	        aecQueue.asUnownedSerialExecutor()
58	    }
59	
60	    // MARK: - Private State
61	
62	    /// Wraps the two Speex C allocations; `nil` after `stop()` or failed init.
63	    private var resources: SpeexResources?
64	
65	    private let frameSize: Int32
66	    private let filterLength: Int32
67	    private let sampleRate: Int32
68	
69	    private let logger = AppLogger.for(category: "AECProcessor")
70	
71	    // MARK: - Pre-allocated frame buffers
72	
73	    private var micInt16: [Int16]
74	    private var farInt16: [Int16]
75	    private var outInt16: [Int16]
76	    private var outFloat: [Float]
77	
78	    // MARK: - Remainder buffer for inter-call chunking
79	
80	    /// Carries sub-frame leftover samples from the previous call.
81	    /// Prepended to the next call's input so no samples are ever discarded.
82	    private var remainder: [Float] = []
83	
84	    // MARK: - Public State
85	
86	    /// `true` while the actor is processing; set to `false` after `stop()`.
87	    public private(set) var isActive = true
88	
89	    // MARK: - Init
90	
91	    public init(frameSize: Int32 = 256, filterLength: Int32 = 4096, sampleRate: Int32 = 16000) {
92	        self.frameSize = frameSize
93	        self.filterLength = filterLength
94	        self.sampleRate = sampleRate
95	
96	        let count = Int(frameSize)
97	        micInt16 = [Int16](repeating: 0, count: count)
98	        farInt16 = [Int16](repeating: 0, count: count)
99	        outInt16 = [Int16](repeating: 0, count: count)
100	        outFloat = [Float](repeating: 0, count: count)
101	
102	        resources = SpeexResources(
103	            frameSize: frameSize,
104	            filterLength: filterLength,
105	            sampleRate: sampleRate
106	        )
107	        if resources == nil {
108	            isActive = false
109	            logger.error("AECProcessorActor: Speex init failed -- AEC is inactive (pass-through mode)")
110	        }
111	    }
112	
113	    // MARK: - Public API
114	
115	    public func process(mic: TaggedAudioBuffer, farEnd: TaggedAudioBuffer) -> TaggedAudioBuffer {
116	        guard let res = resources else {
117	            if !isActive {
118	                logger.warning("AECProcessorActor.process() called after stop() -- returning mic pass-through")
119	            } else {
120	                logger.warning("AECProcessorActor.process() called with nil resources -- returning mic pass-through")
121	            }
122	            return passThrough(mic: mic)
123	        }
124	
125	        let count = Int(frameSize)
126	
127	        // Prepend leftover samples from the previous call, then loop over full
128	        // 256-sample chunks. Speex requires exactly frameSize samples per call;
129	        // the chunking loop ensures every input sample is eventually processed.
130	        var accumulated = remainder + mic.buffer.samples
131	        var allProcessed: [Float] = []
132	        allProcessed.reserveCapacity(accumulated.count)
133	
134	        while accumulated.count >= count {
135	            let chunk = Array(accumulated.prefix(count))
136	            accumulated.removeFirst(count)
137	
138	            fillInt16(&micInt16, from: chunk, frameSize: count)
139	            fillInt16(&farInt16, from: farEnd.buffer.samples, frameSize: count)
140	            for i in 0 ..< count { outInt16[i] = 0 }
141	
142	            speex_echo_cancellation(res.echo, &micInt16, &farInt16, &outInt16)
143	            speex_preprocess_run(res.pp, &outInt16)
144	
145	            fillFloat32(&outFloat, from: outInt16)
146	            allProcessed.append(contentsOf: outFloat)
147	        }
148	
149	        // Carry sub-frame leftovers into the next call.
150	        remainder = accumulated
151	
152	        let outBuffer = AudioBuffer(
153	            sampleRate: Double(sampleRate),
154	            channelCount: 1,
155	            samples: allProcessed,
156	            timestamp: mic.buffer.timestamp
157	        )
158	        return TaggedAudioBuffer(buffer: outBuffer, track: .microphone, timestamp: mic.timestamp)
159	    }
160	
161	    public func stop() {
162	        guard isActive else { return }
163	        isActive = false
164	        resources = nil  // triggers SpeexResources.deinit
165	        remainder = []   // discard buffered remainder -- session is ending
166	        logger.info("AECProcessorActor stopped, Speex resources released")
167	    }

169	    // MARK: - Private Helpers
170	
171	    private func passThrough(mic: TaggedAudioBuffer) -> TaggedAudioBuffer {

## TASK-004: F11 — Update AEC verification harness numbers

**Context:** The AEC buffer chunking fix (F1) is already committed. The Epic-28 AEC verification harness reported numbers based on the broken implementation. Update those numbers to reflect the fix.

**Find the harness/report:**
```
find . -name "*.md" | xargs grep -l "AEC\|aec.*verif\|aec.*harness" 2>/dev/null | grep -v ".build" | head -5
grep -r "aec\|AEC" CHANGELOG.md 2>/dev/null | head -10
```

If no such document exists, skip this task and note it.

**Commit (if changes made):** `docs(F11): update AEC verification numbers to reflect chunking fix`

---

## TASK-005: F2/#191 — Thread a single session ID through the recording pipeline

**Bug:** Three independent ID generation sites all create their own UUIDs:
1. `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.start()` — generates an ID
2. `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.stop()` — generates a different ID  
3. `StartRecordingUseCase.start()` — generates yet another ID

Result: `AudioFile.id != RecordingSession.id` — the invariant INV-001 is violated.

**Find the files:**
```
find . -name "CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.swift" -not -path "*/Tests/*" | head -3
find . -name "StartRecordingUseCase.swift" -not -path "*/Tests/*" | head -3
```

Read both files carefully. Understand where each UUID is generated and how they flow.

**Property INV-001:** `AudioFile.id == RecordingSession.id` for every recording session. One ID generated at `StartRecordingUseCase.start()`, threaded through to all call sites.

**TDD — RED:**
Find or create a test file for StartRecordingUseCase. Write a failing test `testSessionIDThreadedConsistently()` that:
- Mocks CoreAudioTapCaptureActor
- Calls StartRecordingUseCase.start()
- Asserts the session ID used by the tap actor matches the session ID in the returned RecordingSession

Run tests and confirm RED.

**GREEN:**
1. Generate the session ID exactly ONCE in `StartRecordingUseCase.start()` (or wherever the use case first creates the session)
2. Pass that ID explicitly to `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.start(sessionID:)` — update the method signature if needed
3. Remove ID generation from `stop()` and `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.start()` — they receive the ID, not generate it
4. Update all callers of these methods

**REFACTOR + commit:**
```
fix(F2/#191): thread single session ID from StartRecordingUseCase through CoreAudioTap

One UUID generated at use-case start, passed explicitly to all downstream
call sites. Eliminates independent ID generation in start() and stop().

Closes #191
```

**Commit:** `fix(F15): replace force-unwraps in audio pipeline with safe unwrapping`

> These memories may be stale and need verification before you continue:
> - `{name}` ({type}, {age_days} days old) → recommended action: **{action}**
>
> For each: verify it's still accurate, update it, or I'll archive it. Type "skip" to proceed without action.

**Action meanings:**
- `verify` — expired but recent enough that you should confirm it's still accurate
- `archive` — significantly past expiry; move to `{memory_dir}/archive/` rather than delete

Wait for user response before proceeding to Phase 1 (unless the array is empty, in which case proceed immediately).

---

## Phase 1 — Orient

1. List the memory directory to see what topic files already exist
2. Read `MEMORY.md` to understand the current sectioned index (Daily drivers / Project state / Patterns & pitfalls / References)
3. Skim 3–4 of the existing topic files to understand their structure — prevents near-duplicate creation

---

## Phase 2 — Gather recent signal

Look for new information worth persisting.

### 2a: Auto-extraction from transcripts

Find the 2 newest session transcript files:
```
ls -t {transcripts_dir}/*.jsonl | head -2
```

Run the extractor on them:
```
uv run ~/.wfc/skills/wfc-closeout/scripts/memory_extract.py {transcript1} {transcript2}
```

The output has three buckets: `high_confidence`, `medium_confidence`, `low_confidence`.

**High-confidence candidates** (explicit "remember X" / "always do Y" / "never do Z"):
- Auto-write these as memories without asking — they are explicit instructions.
- Write them to the correct section in MEMORY.md based on type.

**Medium-confidence candidates** (corrections, "we should", "actually"):
- Present them to the user in a compact list:
  > Found these potential memories from recent sessions — confirm, skip, or edit each:
  > 1. [suggested_type] "{source_quote}" → save as: `{suggested_name}`?
- Write the ones the user confirms.

**Low-confidence candidates**: skip unless user asks to review them.

### 2b: Manual signal from transcripts

Read the first 50–100 lines of the newest 1–2 transcript files to understand what sessions covered. Then grep narrowly for topics that seem worth persisting:
```
grep -n "term" {transcripts_dir}/{uuid}.jsonl | tail -30
```

> Never read an entire JSONL file. Grep narrowly for things you already suspect matter. These files can be hundreds of megabytes.

### 2c: Drifted memories

Any existing memory file that contradicts what you now see in the codebase or transcripts should be corrected at the source.

### 2d: Episodic detection

Look in transcripts for the pattern: tried X → error/failure → switched to Y. These are candidates for episodic memories in `{memory_dir}/episodic/`.

Signals to grep for: "didn't work", "failed", "wrong", "switched to", "instead I", "turned out".

If you find a clear failure+pivot pattern, write it as an episodic memory (see Episodic Memory section below).

---

## Phase 3 — Consolidate

For each thing worth persisting, write or update a memory file.

### Scope assignment

Before writing, decide scope:
- **Global** (`~/.claude/memory/global/`): Swift language patterns, WFC workflow patterns, general engineering rules that apply across all projects
- **Project** (`{memory_dir}/`): decisions, constraints, deadlines, file paths, epic-specific context

Add `scope: global` or `scope: project` to the `metadata:` block.

### Frontmatter format

```markdown
---
name: short-kebab-case-slug
description: one-line summary — used to decide relevance in future sessions
metadata:
  type: user | feedback | project | reference | episodic
  scope: global | project
  expires_after_days: 60   # project/reference only; omit for feedback/user
  last_verified: YYYY-MM-DD
---

Memory content here.
```

For `feedback` and `project` types, include:
- **Why:** the reason this matters
- **How to apply:** when/where this guidance kicks in

**Merge, don't duplicate**: check existing topic files before creating a new one — similar content should be merged in.

**Absolute dates only**: convert relative dates to absolute dates using today as the anchor.

**Delete, don't annotate**: if an existing memory is wrong, fix or remove it.

**Link related memories**: use `[[slug]]` to reference related topic files.

**What NOT to save**: code patterns, file paths, git history, current task state, or anything already captured in CLAUDE.md.

### Section assignment for MEMORY.md

When writing to project or global MEMORY.md, insert the new pointer into the correct section (not the bottom):

| Type | Section |
|------|---------|
| `feedback` with "always"/"never"/"mandatory" in description | `## Daily drivers` |
| `project` | `## Project state` |
| `feedback` (nuanced, not daily) | `## Patterns & pitfalls` |
| `reference` | `## References` |

Never append to the bottom of an unstructured index. The sections must be preserved.

---

## Episodic Memory

Episodic memories capture specific events: what was tried, why it failed or worked, what the fix was.

Write them to `{memory_dir}/episodic/` (not the main memory dir).

```markdown
---
name: short-slug-epic-N
description: what was tried and what happened
metadata:
  type: episodic
  date: YYYY-MM-DD
  epic: "5.13"
  outcome: success | failure | partial
---
Body: what was tried, the error or failure, what the fix or pivot was.
```

After writing an episodic memory, add a pointer to `{memory_dir}/episodic/INDEX.md`.

---

## Phase 4 — Prune and index

Update `MEMORY.md` to stay **under 200 lines**. It's an index, not a dump.

Each entry is one line:
```
- [Title](file.md) — one-line hook under ~150 chars
```

**Prune**:
- Remove pointers to memories that are stale, superseded, or wrong
- Memories migrated to global scope: remove from project index (global MEMORY.md is loaded separately)
- If an index line is over ~200 characters, shorten it — move the detail to the topic file

**Add**: pointers to newly written or updated topic files, in the correct section

**Resolve**: if two entries contradict each other, fix the wrong one

**Section headers** must be preserved:
```
## Daily drivers (fires every session)
## Project state (time-sensitive)
## Patterns & pitfalls (timeless)
## References (where things live)
```

---

## CLAUDE.md reconciliation

If `{cwd}/CLAUDE.md` exists, review it briefly:
- If a convention in CLAUDE.md conflicts with a stored memory, the memory is wrong — fix it
- CLAUDE.md is authoritative for project conventions

---

## Wrap-up

Report back to the user:
- What was audited and verified/archived (if any)
- What auto-extracted memories were written
- What user-confirmed candidates were written
- What episodic memories were recorded
- What was pruned from the index
- Any CLAUDE.md conflicts that need user attention
- If nothing changed, say so explicitly — don't invent work

User directive (2026-06-12): convert the datum TDD act pipeline into a Workflow script.

Instead of manually launching agents per task/unit, a single Workflow would:

Built. Saved at:
```
~/.claude/projects/-Volumes-Extra-repos-gitrdunhq-the-record-suite/workflows/datum-tdd.js
```

**What it does:**
- **Bootstrap**: reads `tasks.json`, gets live test baseline
- **RED** (parallel): all tasks fan out simultaneously — each RED agent writes a failing test and must confirm it actually fails before returning
- **GREEN** (dependency-aware): parallel units (D/E/F) run concurrently via `parallel()`; serial chain (A→B→C) runs sequentially via a loop — tasks within a unit are sequential to avoid file conflicts
- **REFACTOR**: single final agent runs full suite + swiftlint, validates ratchet floor

**To run it for a future epic:**
```js
Workflow({
  scriptPath: '~/.claude/projects/.../workflows/datum-tdd.js',
  args: { repo: '/path/to/repo', tasks_json: '/path/tasks.json', ratchet_floor: 827 }
})
```

Key design choice: RED agents run in parallel across ALL units regardless of deps (they only write test files, no conflicts), then GREEN respects the dependency graph. This cuts wall-clock time significantly vs serial RED-then-GREEN per task.

unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create \
  --repo gitrdunhq/datum \
  --title "[roadmap] act phase: replace manual agent dispatch with deterministic Workflow orchestration" \
  --label "enhancement" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

The current datum act phase requires manual agent dispatch — launching individual agents per task/unit and supervising them throughout. This creates:

1. **No RED-gate enforcement** — agents can write passing tests in RED stage and proceed to GREEN unchallenged (see #127)
2. **No file-lock coordination** — parallel agents can conflict on shared files (see #129)
3. **Manual dependency tracking** — serial A→B→C ordering must be managed by the orchestrator, not enforced by tooling
4. **Scope violations** — docs agents implement production logic when they have unconstrained file access (see #132)

## Proposed Solution

Convert the act phase into a **deterministic Workflow script** that encodes the full TDD pipeline:

```js
// datum-tdd-act.js
// Reads tasks.json, respects unit dependency graph, enforces RED→GREEN→REFACTOR per task

phase('Topology')
const tasks = await agent('Read tasks.json and return task list with unit membership and depends_on', {schema: TASKS_SCHEMA})

phase('Parallel units')
// D, E, F have no serial dependencies — run concurrently
const [dResult, eResult, fResult] = await parallel([
  () => runUnit('unit-d', tasks),
  () => runUnit('unit-e', tasks),
  () => runUnit('unit-f', tasks),
])

phase('Serial audio path')
// A → B → C must run in order
await runUnit('unit-a', tasks)
await runUnit('unit-b', tasks)
await runUnit('unit-c', tasks)

// runUnit() fans out tasks in that unit, each through:
//   RED agent → verify tests FAIL (hard stop if they pass) → GREEN agent → verify tests PASS → commit
```

## Key Enforcements the Workflow Provides

- **RED verification**: after RED agent commits, run `swift test --filter <new_test>` and assert non-zero exit. If tests pass → halt with `green_blindness_violation` (resolves #127)
- **File-ownership sandbox**: each task agent is told exactly which files it may write (`task.files[]`). Workflow verifies no other files were touched before GREEN dispatch (resolves #129, #132)
- **Ratchet gate**: after every GREEN, verify test count ≥ ratchet floor before proceeding
- **Protocol conformance check**: after any method signature change, grep for all conforming types and verify they compile

## Implementation Notes

- Save as `.claude/workflows/datum-tdd-act.js` (or similar) in the datum skill dir
- `args` accepts: `{ tasks_json_path, ratchet_floor, model_haiku, model_sonnet, package_paths }`
- Per-task model assignment from `tasks.json` (add `model_tier: "haiku"|"sonnet"` field)
- Isolation: `isolation: 'worktree'` per task to prevent cross-task file conflicts
- On failure: log to `.datum/act-failures.jsonl`, continue other units, surface summary at end

## Context

Filed during epic-30 (datum/epic-30-audit-remediation) where the manual dispatch approach produced 8 datum friction issues (#125–#132) and required constant mid-flight corrections. A Workflow would have caught most of these automatically.

Related: #127 (RED gate), #128 (target import context), #129 (file-lock), #131 (SourceKit false positives), #132 (docs scope)
EOF

1	# THE RECORD — Agent Instructions
2	
3	Local-first meeting transcription app. macOS 15+ (shipped) · Windows/Linux (roadmap). Swift 6.2, Clean Architecture, TDD.
4	
5	This file is the universal entry point for ALL AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Aider, etc.). Tool-specific configs (`.claude/`, `.cursorrules`, `.opencode.yaml`) extend this — they don't replace it.
6	
7	## Resume
8	
9	Read `CURRENT_STATE.md` — it has the current epic, phase, next action, and session handoff state.
10	If you are a human developer, start with `ONBOARDING.md`.
11	
12	## GRAPHIFY FIRST (MANDATORY)
13	
14	Before any research, planning, or implementation, you MUST ensure the knowledge graphs are up-to-date:
15	```bash
16	./scripts/graphify_suite.sh
17	```
18	- **Code Graph**: `graphify-code/graph.html` (Sources only)
19	- **Test Graph**: `graphify-tests/graph.html` (Tests only)
20	
21	Open the relevant HTML and read the `GRAPH_REPORT.md` in each directory. Use `graphify query --graph graphify-code/graph.json` for architectural questions.
22	
23	## Codebase-Wide Invariants (MANDATORY)
24	
25	Every agent MUST adhere to these 10 core invariants. See `docs/architecture/INVARIANTS.md` for details.
26	
27	1.  **Actor isolation prevents races** — everywhere you have shared mutable state.
28	2.  **No meeting content in telemetry/public logs** — never log user content at `.public`.
29	3.  **INSERT OR IGNORE / Idempotent writes** — everywhere DuckDB is touched.
30	4.  **Buffer only cleared on success** — any buffered flush pattern.
31	5.  **Existing API signatures unchanged** — preserve compatibility during refactors.
32	6.  **No network egress / Local-first** — user data stays on-device.
33	7.  **Explicit OSLog privacy labels** — every interpolation needs a label.
34	8.  **All existing tests must pass** — count never decreases.
35	9.  **No logic changes during structural refactors** — move first, then modify.
36	10. **Weak self in ViewModel Tasks** — prevent memory leaks.
37	
38	## Architecture (4-Layer Clean)
39	
40	```
41	Domain (structs, enums, protocols)  ←  Business (actors)  ←  Infrastructure (actors)
42	                                    ←  Presentation (@MainActor classes)
43	```
44	
45	### Layer Import Rules (STRICT)
46	
47	| Layer | Allowed Imports | File Limit |
48	|-------|----------------|------------|
49	| Domain | `Foundation` only | 100 lines |
50	| Business | Domain + Foundation + OSLog | 300 lines |
51	| Infrastructure | Domain + any framework (CoreAudio, DuckDB, WhisperKit, etc.) | 300 lines |
52	| Presentation | Domain + Business + SwiftUI | ViewModels: 200, Views: 150 |
53	
54	Presentation NEVER imports Infrastructure directly. Business NEVER imports Infrastructure. Domain NEVER imports anything except Foundation.
55	
56	### Key Patterns
57	
58	- **Actors** for all shared mutable state (Swift 6.2 strict concurrency)
59	- **@MainActor** for Presentation layer (ViewModels and Views)
60	- **@Observable** for ViewModels (NOT ObservableObject)
61	- **Protocol seams** between layers — Infrastructure implements Domain protocols
62	- **All external errors translated** to domain errors at the Infrastructure boundary
63	- **No `@unchecked Sendable`** except `Infrastructure/Audio/` and `Domain/Audio/AudioBuffer.swift`
64	
65	## Functional Core / Imperative Shell
66	
67	Business logic (the Business layer) must be expressed as pure transformations: given the same inputs, produce the same outputs, with no hidden side effects. All side effects — persistence, audio I/O, network, calendar writes — live in Infrastructure actors at the edge of the system. This is the principle that makes the layer import rules meaningful: if Business could call Infrastructure directly, side effects would bleed into logic and tests would require full infrastructure setup.
68	
69	## Boundary Validation
70	
71	Validate the shape of all external inputs immediately at the boundary where they enter the system — IPC payloads, deserialized JSON/DuckDB rows, file-parsed data, MCP server responses. No business logic executes on unvalidated payloads. In Swift, this means decoding to a typed struct/enum at the Infrastructure boundary and returning a domain error if decoding fails — never passing raw `[String: Any]` into Business or Domain.
72	
73	## File Size Cap
74	
75	Hard cap: **500 lines per file** across the entire codebase (layer limits are stricter — see the layer table; this is the absolute ceiling). When a file approaches the limit, split it at a functional seam, never at an arbitrary line count. Extracting a protocol or a sub-actor is preferred over creating a `+Extension` file that just shuffles lines.
76	
77	## Coding Standards — Resiliency
78	
79	- **Timeouts & retries.** Every external call (HTTP, DB, subprocess, XPC) must have an explicit timeout and capped-backoff retry. Never fire-and-forget external I/O.
80	- **Idempotency.** All mutating operations must be idempotent — use upserts or dedup checks before side effects. (Swift-specific: `INSERT OR IGNORE` for DuckDB — already an invariant, applies broadly.)
81	- **Explicit state.** Represent state as enums or literals. State transitions must be guarded and explicit — no implicit boolean flags that grow over time.
82	- **Structured errors.** Errors are never silently swallowed. At API / IPC boundaries, errors must carry a code, a human-readable message, and a correlation ID so failures are traceable.
83	- **No silent fallbacks.** Never use nil-coalescing (`??`) or short-circuit (`||`) to substitute a default when the data should not be missing. Fail fast and surface the problem.
84	
85	## No Invented APIs
86	
87	Do not call APIs, methods, types, or SPM packages that you have not confirmed exist in the codebase or in official documentation. Before using any symbol you did not write yourself:
88	1. Search the codebase for its definition.
89	2. If it is an external dependency, confirm it exists in the current version declared in `Package.swift`.
90	Hallucinating a symbol and then implementing it to make the call compile is a violation of this rule.
91	
92	## Minimal Diffs
93	
94	Only change what is required by the current task. No drive-by rewrites, style normalizations, or unrequested refactors in the same commit. If you spot a problem outside the task scope, open a GitHub issue to track it — do not fix it silently in the same diff.
95	
96	## Preserve Diagnostic Logging
97	
98	Never remove or silence diagnostic log statements in the same commit as a bug fix. If a log is noisy, reduce its level or mark it for cleanup in a dedicated follow-up commit — but keep it present when the fix lands so the fix can be observed.
99	
100	## Validate Before Applying at Scale
101	
102	Before applying generated code or mechanical changes across many files:
103	1. Apply to **one file first** and verify it builds and tests pass.
104	2. Break large batches into testable chunks of ≤10 files.
105	3. For anything with syntax risk (templates, string interpolations, shell scripts), dry-run or compile-check before applying broadly.
106	
107	Never apply unvalidated output to 10+ files in a single pass.
108	
109	## No Re-Planning Completed Work
110	
111	Do not re-plan, re-explore, or re-research any phase of work that has already been completed in the current session or is marked complete in CURRENT_STATE.md / TASKS.md. If you are unsure whether something is done, check CURRENT_STATE.md or ask — do not restart from scratch.
112	
113	## See Something, Say Something
114	
115	When you encounter a bug, security issue, broken assumption, or missing test outside the current task scope — do not ignore it and do not fix it in-scope. Open a GitHub issue to track it:
116	
117	```bash
118	unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create \
119	  --title "[see-something] category: brief description (file:line)" \
120	  --label "see-something" \
121	  --body "What is wrong, why it matters, and suggested fix."
122	```
123	
124	Deduplicate: search open issues before creating a new one. Severity threshold: anything that could cause data loss, a crash, a security breach, or a silent correctness failure.
125	
126	## Active TODO (Mandatory)
127	
128	**Always keep at least one task active in the TaskList tool during any coding session.**
129	
130	Before starting work: create tasks for every step. Mark each `in_progress` when you start it. Mark `completed` the moment it's done. Never let the list go empty mid-session — if you finish a task and have more work, create the next one before marking the current one complete.
131	
132	This keeps the user informed at a glance. A session with no tasks is a session with no visibility.
133	
134	## TDD Order (MANDATORY)
135	
136	```
137	1. Write test → 2. Verify it FAILS (RED) → 3. Implement → 4. Verify it PASSES (GREEN) → 5. Commit together
138	```
139	
140	Never write implementation before the test. Never skip the RED step. Tests use Swift Testing framework (`@Suite`, `@Test`, `#expect`), NOT XCTest.
141	
142	## Build & Test
143	
144	```bash
145	swift build                    # debug build
146	swift build -c release         # release build
147	swift test                     # run all tests (1479+ tests, ~5.2s)
148	swift test --filter SuiteName  # run specific test suite
149	```
150	
151	**Sub-package test gotcha:** `swift test --filter` from the repo root only reaches Record-App-hosted test targets. Tests in `Record-Audio/Tests/` and `Record-ML/Tests/` must be run from inside that sub-package (`cd Record-Audio && swift test --filter SuiteName`) — from the root the filter silently matches 0 tests and reports success.
152	
153	## Maintenance Tools
154	
155	- **Invariants Analysis**: Run `python3 scripts/analyze_properties.py` to identify predicates appearing in 5+ epics for promotion to `docs/architecture/INVARIANTS.md`.
156	
157	## Semantic Memory (ChromaDB)
158	
159	Query BEFORE implementing — check for prior art, prior fixes, and reviewed patterns.
160	
161	| Collection | Docs | Contains |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| `architecture_knowledge` | 261 | Architecture analysis, SwiftUI patterns, skill references |
164	| `agentic_knowledge` | 4117 | Solution docs, review reports, test strategies, prior fixes |
165	
166	**Query** (run from any shell):
167	
168	```bash
169	~/.agents/chroma_env/bin/python3 -c "
170	import chromadb, os
171	client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path=os.path.expanduser('~/.agents/chromadb/'))
172	col = client.get_collection('agentic_knowledge')
173	results = col.query(query_texts=['YOUR QUERY HERE'], n_results=5)
174	for doc, meta in zip(results['documents'][0], results['metadatas'][0]):
175	    print(meta.get('source',''), '\n', doc[:300], '\n---')
176	"
177	```
178	
179	- Query `architecture_knowledge` for layer design, protocol shape, or SwiftUI patterns.
180	- Query `agentic_knowledge` for prior bug fixes, solution docs, or review findings.
181	- **Ingest new references:** `.agents/ingest_references.py` — place `.md` files in `.agents/references/`.
182	
183	## Git Commits
184	
185	Format: `Epic {N}: [{Layer}] {Description}`
186	
187	Additional constraints:
188	- **No tool attribution.** Never add "Co-Authored-By: \<AI tool\>" or any AI/vendor attribution to commit messages.
189	- **Squash before first push.** Before the branch has a remote tracking branch or open PR, squash all local commits into one (`git rebase -i origin/main`). One commit per PR at open time.
190	- **Additive after publish.** Once a branch has a PR open, never rebase, amend, squash, or force-push. Stack new commits on top for review fixups.
191	- **Never force-push main/master.**
192	
193	## Git Operations Default Scope
194	
195	Default to **local-only** git operations: commit, branch, merge, tag. Do NOT push to remote, create PRs, open issues, or perform any remote git operation unless the user explicitly requests it in the current session.
196	
197	## Project Layout
198	
199	Single root `Package.swift` — `swift build` / `swift test` from repo root.
200	
201	```
202	Sources:
203	  Record-Foundation/Sources/Domain/              ← Domain layer (Foundation only)
204	  Record-Foundation/Sources/Logging/             ← Logging (Domain-tier, OSLog wrapper)
205	  Record-Audio/Sources/AudioInfrastructure/      ← Audio capture I/O (CoreAudio, AVFoundation, CSpeex)
206	  Record-ML/Sources/MLInfrastructure/            ← ML inference + Storage (WhisperKit, MLX, DuckDB)
207	    Storage/                                         ← DuckDB persistence
208	    Transcription/                                   ← WhisperKit transcription
209	    Diarization/                                     ← FluidAudio speaker diarization
210	    Summarization/                                   ← MLX summarization
211	  Record-App/Sources/Business/                   ← Business layer (actors, use cases)
212	  Record-App/Sources/TheRecord/                  ← Executable: composition root
213	  Record-Presentation/Sources/Presentation/      ← Presentation layer (SwiftUI)
214	  Record-Pro/Sources/RecordPro/                  ← RecordPro (Pro tier: DTW, xgrammar)
215	
216	Tests:
217	  Record-Foundation/Tests/Unit/Domain/              → DomainTests
218	  Record-Audio/Tests/Unit/                          → AudioInfrastructureTests
219	  Record-ML/Tests/Unit/                             → MLInfrastructureTests
220	    Storage/
221	    Mocks/
222	  Record-App/Tests/Unit/Business/                   → BusinessTests
223	  Record-App/Tests/Unit/Infrastructure/             → AppInfrastructureTests
224	  Record-Presentation/Tests/Unit/Presentation/      → PresentationTests
225	  Record-App/Tests/Unit/Presentation/               → AppPresentationTests
226	
227	Isolated (cross-platform, macOS 15+, no heavy deps):
228	  Record-CrossPlatform-Foundation/                  ← Future Windows/Linux work
229	```
230	
231	Sub-packages (`Record-Foundation/`, `Record-Audio/`, `Record-ML/`, `Record-App/`, etc.) remain valid standalone builds.
232	
233	## Skills (Progressive Disclosure)
234	
235	Skills are detailed instruction sets for each architectural layer. Read the relevant skill BEFORE writing code for that layer. Skills are in `.claude/skills/` but the content is universal — any agent can read them.
